title: Symmetric algebra images of a finitely presented module system cover affine sections
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal A$ a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf] whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preordered set (every pair has a common upper bound). Let $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i})_{i\le i'}$ be a system of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, each of finite presentation, meaning locally the cokernel of a map $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}$ with finite $m,n$. Suppose compatible $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\varphi_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal A$ exhibit the underlying module of $\mathcal A$ as their colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Then each $\mathcal F_i$ is quasi-coherent. Let $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F_i)$ be the explicitly constructed symmetric algebra sheaf of $\mathcal F_i$ (the sheafification of $U\mapsto\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal F_i(U)$) and $j_i:\mathcal F_i\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F_i)$ its degree-one map [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction]. Then there is a unique algebra map $\psi_i:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F_i)\to\mathcal A$ with $\psi_i j_i=\varphi_i$. Let $\mathcal C_i\subseteq\mathcal A$ be its sheaf image, whose sections are sections locally in the image of $\psi_i$. Each $\mathcal C_i$ is a quasi-coherent algebra subsheaf of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-quasi-coherent-subalgebras]. For every affine open $U$, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, one has $\mathcal C_i(U)=\psi_{i,U}(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F_i)(U))$; $\mathcal F_i(U)$ is finitely presented over $R$, and any finite module generating list $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ for it yields the algebra generating list $\varphi_{i,U}(f_1),\ldots,\varphi_{i,U}(f_n)$ for $\mathcal C_i(U)$. Moreover, for every $a\in\mathcal A(U)$ there exist $i\in I$ and $x\in\mathcal F_i(U)$ such that $a=\varphi_{i,U}(x)=\psi_{i,U}(j_{i,U}(x))\in\mathcal C_i(U)$.

proof.text: For each $i$, apply clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] to the given local finite presentation of $\mathcal F_i$. Thus $\mathcal F_i$ is quasi-coherent. Fix any affine open $U$ and put $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$. Finite presentation is local, so $\mathcal F_i|_U$ is still of finite presentation; clause (b) of the same node gives that $M_i=\mathcal F_i(U)$ is a finitely presented $R$-module. In particular it is finitely generated: in a presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M_i\to0$, the images of the $n$ standard basis vectors generate $M_i$.

Use the explicit symmetric algebra sheaf $S_i=P_i^\#$ and degree-one map $j_i$ of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core] with $F=\mathcal F_i$, $B=\mathcal A$, and $f=\varphi_i$. This gives exactly one algebra-sheaf morphism $\psi_i:S_i\to\mathcal A$ with $\psi_i j_i=\varphi_i$. Since $\mathcal F_i$ is quasi-coherent by Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-affine] gives that $S_i$ is quasi-coherent and, for every affine $U$, the algebra map $\theta_{i,U}:\operatorname{Sym}_R(M_i)\to S_i(U)$ is bijective. By the definition of $j_i$ in the construction, $\theta_{i,U}(\iota_{M_i}(x))=j_{i,U}(x)$.

source.place: Section 01CF, section-symmetric-exterior; Tag 01CG, lemma-local-tensor-algebra; Tag 01CL, lemma-whole-tensor-algebra-permanence

proof.text: Both $S_i$ and $\mathcal A$ have quasi-coherent underlying modules, and $\psi_i$ is an algebra map. Clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal] therefore applies. Its image is precisely the subsheaf $\mathcal C_i$ defined in the item, because both are defined by local membership in the image of $\psi_i$. It is a quasi-coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-algebra of $\mathcal A$, and for every affine open $U$ its sections satisfy $\mathcal C_i(U)=\psi_{i,U}(S_i(U))$. This uses affine exactness from that cited statement, rather than assuming that an arbitrary sheaf image is a sectionwise image.

source.place: Tag 01IC, lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent; Section 01LA, section-quasi-coherent, items (1) and (5); Properties Tag 05JT, lemma-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-type, image argument

proof.text: Fix an affine $U$ and any finite module generating list $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ for $M_i$. Clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-presentation] says that $\iota_{M_i}(f_1),\ldots,\iota_{M_i}(f_n)$ generate $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M_i)$ as an $R$-algebra. For any $c\in\mathcal C_i(U)$, Step 3 supplies $s\in S_i(U)$ with $\psi_{i,U}(s)=c$; Step 2 supplies $t\in\operatorname{Sym}_R(M_i)$ with $\theta_{i,U}(t)=s$. Write $t$ as a polynomial $P$ over $R$ in those degree-one generators. Since $\psi_i$ and $\theta_{i,U}$ are algebra maps, $c=P(\varphi_{i,U}(f_1),\ldots,\varphi_{i,U}(f_n))$. Conversely these elements belong to $\mathcal C_i(U)$ by Steps 2 and 3. Thus they generate $\mathcal C_i(U)$. Step 1 provides such a finite list for every affine $U$; together with quasi-coherence from Step 3, this is exactly the finite type subalgebra condition of [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-quasi-coherent-subalgebras].

source.place: Section 00DM, section-tensor-algebra, generation by products of degree-one elements; Properties Tag 05JT, lemma-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-type, definition preceding the lemma

proof.text: The given maps $\varphi_i$ form a colimit cocone in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, the index is a nonempty directed set, and every $\mathcal F_i$ is quasi-coherent by Step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-affine-sections] to this very cocone. For every affine $U$ and every $a\in\mathcal A(U)$, its element-representative clause gives $i\in I$ and $x\in\mathcal F_i(U)$ with $a=\varphi_{i,U}(x)$. The identity $\psi_i j_i=\varphi_i$ from Step 2 gives $a=\psi_{i,U}(j_{i,U}(x))$, and Step 3 places this element in $\mathcal C_i(U)$. This proves the last clause with the actual given maps, not just an abstract colimit isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem symmetricImagesModuleColimit (X : Scheme.{u}) (A : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) (hA : A.toModule.IsQuasicoherent) (I : Type u) [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (F : I ⥤ X.Modules) (hF : ∀ i : I, (F.obj i).IsFinitePresentation) (φ : F ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj A.toModule) (hc : IsColimit (Cocone.mk A.toModule φ)) : (∀ i : I, (F.obj i).IsQuasicoherent) ∧ ∃ (ψ : ∀ i : I, SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.algebra (F.obj i) ⟶ A) (C : I → A.finiteTypeQuasiCoherentSubalgebras), (∀ i : I, (∀ (U : X.Opens) (x : (F.obj i).val.obj (op U)), (ψ i).right.hom.app (op U) ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.inclusion (F.obj i)).val.app (op U) x) = (φ.app i).val.app (op U) x) ∧ (∀ t : SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.algebra (F.obj i) ⟶ A, (∀ (U : X.Opens) (x : (F.obj i).val.obj (op U)), t.right.hom.app (op U) ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.inclusion (F.obj i)).val.app (op U) x) = (φ.app i).val.app (op U) x) → t = ψ i) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (s : A.right.obj.obj (op U)), s ∈ Set.range ((C i).val.arrow.right.hom.app (op U)) ↔ ∀ p : X, p ∈ U → ∃ (V : X.Opens) (hVU : V ≤ U), p ∈ V ∧ A.right.obj.map (homOfLE hVU).op s ∈ Set.range ((ψ i).right.hom.app (op V))) ∧ (∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → Set.range ((C i).val.arrow.right.hom.app (op U)) = Set.range ((ψ i).right.hom.app (op U)) ∧ Module.FinitePresentation Γ(X, U) Γ(F.obj i, U) ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → Γ(F.obj i, U)), Submodule.span Γ(X, U) (Set.range f) = ⊤ → (↑(@Algebra.adjoin Γ(X, U) (A.right.obj.obj (op U)) _ _ (A.hom.hom.app (op U)).hom.toAlgebra (Set.range (fun k : Fin n ↦ (φ.app i).val.app (op U) (f k)))) : Set (A.right.obj.obj (op U))) = Set.range ((C i).val.arrow.right.hom.app (op U)))) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → ∀ a : A.right.obj.obj (op U), ∃ (i : I) (x : Γ(F.obj i, U)), a = (φ.app i).val.app (op U) x ∧ a = (ψ i).right.hom.app (op U) ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.inclusion (F.obj i)).val.app (op U) x) ∧ a ∈ Set.range ((C i).val.arrow.right.hom.app (op U)))
